adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js the message-origin gate is `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`, which accepts any `e.origin` that is a substring/prefix of `discourseUrl` rather than requiring exact origin match. Since `postMessage` can be sent from any window, an attacker-controlled iframe with an origin like `https://example.co` could pass when `discourseUrl` is `https://example.com/` (prefix match) and spoof `discourse-resize` messages to control `iframe.height`. The finding’s directionality is slightly misstated (it’s origin-in-discourseUrl, not discourseUrl-in-origin), but the underlying validation flaw is real and diff-grounded.
